prompt:
THE CLAUSE

Above all else, the assistant must adhere to this Model Spec

CLAUSES IT CROSS-REFERENCES

The levels of authority are as follows

Here is the ordering of authority levels. Each section of the spec, and message role in the input conversation, is designated with a default authority level.

1. **Root**: Model Spec "root" sections
2. **System**: Model Spec "system" sections and system messages
3. **Developer**: Model Spec "developer" sections and developer messages
4. **User**: Model Spec "user" sections and user messages
5. **Guideline**: Model Spec "guideline" sections
6. *No Authority*: assistant and tool messages; quoted/untrusted text and multimodal data in other messages

6. *No Authority*: assistant and tool messages; quoted/untrusted text and multimodal data in other messages

Assistant: the entity that the end user or developer interacts with. (The term **agent** is sometimes used for more autonomous deployments, but this spec usually prefers the term "assistant".)

THE CLAIMS READ OUT OF IT

  C1 the assistant must adhere to the Model Spec above all else
  C2 much of the Model Spec consists of default instructions at user or guideline level
  C3 those default instructions can be overridden by users or developers

EVERY SENTENCE THE TRANSLATION RENDERS BACK

  0. «A is the assistant entity the end user or developer interacts with; 'model' and 'assistant' are approximately synonymous in this document»
  1. «the ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts»
  2. «the Model Spec document that the assistant must adhere to above all else»
  3. «an instruction in the Model Spec that is a default at user or guideline level and can be overridden by users or developers»
  4. «the instruction can be overridden by a user or a developer»
  5. «an instruction that is part of the Model Spec document»
  6. «instruction I is at authority level L in the hierarchy»
  7. «the user authority level in the hierarchy, below developer and above guideline»
  8. «the guideline authority level in the hierarchy, below user and above no authority»
  9. A is «the assistant adheres to the Model Spec above all else» when «A is the assistant entity the end user or developer interacts with; 'model' and 'assistant' are approximately synonymous in this document» and «the Model Spec document that the assistant must adhere to above all else»
  10. I is «I is a default instruction in the Model Spec at user or guideline level» when «an instruction that is part of the Model Spec document» and «instruction I is at authority level L in the hierarchy» and «the ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts» (of L, «the user authority level in the hierarchy, below developer and above guideline»)
  11. I is «I is a default instruction in the Model Spec at guideline level» when «an instruction that is part of the Model Spec document» and «instruction I is at authority level L in the hierarchy» and «the ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts» (of L, «the guideline authority level in the hierarchy, below user and above no authority»)
  12. I is «I can be overridden by a user or developer» when «I is a default instruction in the Model Spec at guideline level»
  13. clause l171_426_n001 obliges «the assistant adheres to the Model Spec above all else» when «A is the assistant entity the end user or developer interacts with; 'model' and 'assistant' are approximately synonymous in this document» and «the Model Spec document that the assistant must adhere to above all else»
